protocol.propose: proposer=bright,houghpeaks,radon; geometry re-measured by PCA of the pixels behind each candidate
protocol.cross_ccd: shared-CRVAL per-CCD TAN WCS maps every CCD into one tangent plane; the gnomonic projection maps great circles to straight lines, so a real trail is one collinear line on every CCD it crosses
protocol.chip_replica: a sky line lands at a different CCD-local offset on each chip, so members sharing a CCD-local line are replicated per chip (chip edges, serial-register rows)
protocol.static_structure: identical CRVAL means identical WCS, so detector-fixed structure repeats at the same CCD pixels in another epoch of the same pointing; real trails move
protocol.axis_veto: a candidate within 1.5 deg of a CCD axis sitting on a column/row whose robust noise is an outlier for that chip
protocol.independent_measurement: bilinear profile along the candidate line against a background band 25-60 px off-line in raw counts; support_px is the longest run above 4 sigma

data_requirements.note: The MegaCam exposures are not committed (benchmark_data/ is gitignored); this fixture stores geometry and provenance only.
data_requirements.merge_note: Two invocations, merged by exposure (see `provenance`): a single invocation over all ten local exposures exceeds a practical runtime because every Radon candidate is scored with a full along-line profile. Each invocation kept >=3 exposures of the same CCD set, which is what the persistence layer needs.

_run.note: Three epochs of one pointing (QW322, 2008-08-02), 36 CCDs each: the persistence layer is at full strength because a bad column is a property of the chip and 1013719p/20p/21p share both the pointing and the CCD set.

runs.note: Three epochs of one pointing (QW322, 2008-08-02), 36 CCDs each: the persistence layer is at full strength because a bad column is a property of the chip and 1013719p/20p/21p share both the pointing and the CCD set.

runs.command: pixi run python benchmarks/curate_trail_truth.py --data-root benchmark_data/megacam --exposures megacam_streak_case --workers 4 --out ...
runs.note: The 2017 40-CCD format (megacam_streak_case, 136 s r-band), so the compiled label set covers both MegaCam readout formats. No second epoch of this pointing exists locally, so its persistence layer cannot fire.

provenance.labels_are: artefact + trail only; the ~1700 uncertain entries are in the review sheet, not here

finding.statement: No candidate in the locally available MegaCam exposures survives curation as a real satellite/aircraft trail. Four independent proposers (bright elongated connected components, the binned-Hough prescreen, the production detect_streaks mask, and an exhaustive binned Radon sweep) were run over ten exposures and 364 HDUs, and every long bright line resolves to a chip-level defect.
measured: CCD 8351-11-4 of megacam_streak_case has 3072 of its 4644 rows above 20 sigma in column x=1830 -- 66% of the column: a bad column, not a trail.
CCD 8352-3-5 has 3675 of 4644 rows above 20 sigma in column x=1922 (79%).
Every chip in both readout formats carries a bright band at y ~ 4590, roughly 50 px from the array edge, across the full 2112-px width.
The only cross-CCD mosaic coincidences found were between such structures: chip-vertical lines on mirrored chips, which the chip_replica and along-line-connectivity tests reject.

The production detect_streaks positives on 1013719p (30,416 mask pixels over 7 CCDs, 19,151 on one) are consistent with a single full-height chip-column band (~4,600 x 4 px = 18,400 px), not with a trail.
finding.consequence: This label set is therefore a false-positive benchmark: it scores a detector on the real clutter it must NOT mask. It cannot yet score trail recall -- that needs a field that actually contains a trail, curated with the same tool.
